modules.title: Phishing Detection & Awareness
modules.description: Learn to identify and prevent phishing attacks, one of the most common cyber threats.

questions.question: What is a common sign of a phishing email?
options: The email comes from a known sender
The email contains urgent language asking for immediate action
The email has perfect spelling and grammar
The email offers a legitimate discount
questions.explanation: Phishing emails often create a false sense of urgency to trick you into acting quickly without thinking.

questions.question: What should you do if you receive a suspicious email?
options: Click the link to see where it goes
Reply and ask for more information
Report it to your IT security team
Forward it to all your colleagues
questions.explanation: Always report suspicious emails to your security team. They have tools to analyze them safely.

questions.question: What is "spear phishing"?
options: A phishing attack targeting random people
A phishing attack targeting a specific individual or organization
A phishing attack sent via SMS
A phishing attack using phone calls
questions.explanation: Spear phishing is highly targeted, using personal information to appear legitimate to specific victims.

questions.question: What does HTTPS indicate in a website URL?
options: The website is completely safe and verified
The connection between your browser and the website is encrypted
The website cannot be hacked
The website is from a government organization
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts data between you and the website, but doesn't guarantee the website itself is legitimate.

questions.question: Which of these is a red flag in an email?
options: Generic greeting like "Dear Customer"
Your actual name in the greeting
A known company logo
Proper spelling and grammar
questions.explanation: Legitimate companies usually address you by name. Generic greetings are a common phishing tactic.

questions.question: What is "whaling" in cybersecurity?
options: A phishing attack targeting executives or high-profile individuals
A type of computer virus that spreads through email
A method of encrypting sensitive data
A network security protocol for wireless connections
questions.explanation: Whaling targets "big fish" like CEOs and CFOs to gain access to sensitive company information.

questions.question: What should you check before clicking a link in an email?
options: The sender's display name only
Hover over the link to see the actual URL
The email subject line only
The time the email was sent
questions.explanation: Hovering reveals the true destination URL. Fake links often look legitimate but point to malicious sites.

questions.question: What is domain spoofing?
options: Creating a website that looks identical to a legitimate one
Speeding up your internet connection
A type of antivirus software
A method to recover deleted emails
questions.explanation: Attackers create fake websites with similar domain names (e.g., amaz0n.com instead of amazon.com).

modules.title: Malware Analysis & Protection
modules.description: Understand different types of malware and how to protect against them.

questions.question: What type of malware locks your files and demands payment for release?
options: Virus
Trojan
Ransomware
Spyware
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts your files and demands a ransom (usually cryptocurrency) for the decryption key.

questions.question: What is a "Trojan Horse" in cybersecurity?
options: A virus that spreads rapidly through email
A worm that self-replicates across networks
Malware disguised as legitimate software
A type of hardware firewall device
questions.explanation: Trojans trick users by appearing as legitimate software while carrying malicious payloads.

questions.question: Which of these is a common way malware spreads?
options: Email attachments
Software downloads
USB drives
All of the above
questions.explanation: Malware can spread through multiple vectors. Always be cautious with any external files or devices.

questions.question: What does a keylogger do?
options: Logs and records every keystroke you make
Deletes all your files permanently
Encrypts your data for ransom
Slows down your computer performance
questions.explanation: Keyloggers capture passwords, credit card numbers, and sensitive information typed on your keyboard.

questions.question: What is a computer worm?
options: Malware that requires user interaction to spread
Malware that self-replicates across networks without user interaction
A type of antivirus software
A hardware security device
questions.explanation: Worms spread automatically across networks, causing damage without any user action.

questions.question: What is a "zero-day" vulnerability?
options: A vulnerability that has existed for zero days (just discovered)
A vulnerability that only works at midnight
A vulnerability that affects only old software
A vulnerability that cannot be exploited
questions.explanation: Zero-day vulnerabilities are unknown to software vendors, giving zero days to prepare a fix.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of malware infection?
options: Computer running very slowly
Unexpected pop-up windows
Files being encrypted or deleted
All of the above
questions.explanation: Multiple symptoms can indicate infection. Run regular antivirus scans if you notice these signs.

questions.question: What is a botnet?
options: A network of compromised computers controlled by an attacker
A type of antivirus software
A robot used for physical security
A network security protocol
questions.explanation: Botnets are used for DDoS attacks, spam distribution, and other malicious activities.

modules.title: Network Security Fundamentals
modules.description: Master the fundamentals of securing computer networks.

questions.question: What does a firewall do?
options: Speeds up your internet connection
Blocks unauthorized network traffic based on rules
Encrypts all data on your computer
Creates automatic backups of your files
questions.explanation: Firewalls act as gatekeepers, allowing or blocking traffic based on predefined security rules.

questions.question: What is a VPN (Virtual Private Network) used for?
options: To make your computer run faster
To securely connect to a private network over the internet
To block all online advertisements
To clean your hard drive of temporary files
questions.explanation: VPNs create encrypted tunnels, protecting your data from interception on public networks.

questions.question: What is a DDoS attack?
options: A virus that deletes system files
Overwhelming a server with traffic to make it unavailable
Stealing passwords through fake websites
Encrypting data and demanding a ransom
questions.explanation: DDoS attacks flood targets with traffic, exhausting resources and causing service outages.

questions.question: What does WPA stand for in WiFi security?
options: Wireless Protected Access
Wired Privacy Authentication
Web Protection Algorithm
WiFi Personal Access
questions.explanation: WPA is the standard for securing wireless networks. Always use WPA2 or WPA3 for security.

questions.question: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
options: 80 (HTTP)
443 (HTTPS)
8080 (Proxy)
22 (SSH)
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses port 443. HTTP uses port 80. Secure websites should use HTTPS on port 443.

questions.question: What is a MAC address?
options: A unique identifier for network devices
An Apple computer model
A type of encryption algorithm
A network protocol for email
questions.explanation: MAC addresses are factory-assigned unique identifiers for every network interface card.

questions.question: What is DNS (Domain Name System)?
options: A security protocol for websites
The system that translates domain names to IP addresses
A type of firewall rule
A virus scanning technique
questions.explanation: DNS is like the phonebook of the internet, converting human-readable names to IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the "principle of least privilege"?
options: Giving users only the minimum access needed to do their job
Making all passwords as short as possible
Using the least expensive security solutions
Having minimal security to maximize convenience
questions.explanation: This principle limits damage by restricting unnecessary access. Users get only what they need.
